extracted.intended_audience: researchers, authors, journal editors, and systematic reviewers working with observational epidemiologic studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation of how the STROBE statement (a 22-item checklist) should be used to report cohort, case–control and cross-sectional studies, and how citations of STROBE in the literature should be interpreted/classified.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE recommendations (22-item checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) recommendations consist of a checklist of 22 items that provide guidance on the reporting of cohort, case–control and cross-sectional studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to facilitate critical appraisal and interpretation of results. (As stated: 'checklist of 22 items' for cohort, case–control and cross-sectional studies; published October 2007 in several leading journals.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use: guide reporting of observational studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Using STROBE to guide the reporting of observational studies is considered an appropriate use of the statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors explicitly classify 'the use of STROBE to guide the reporting of observational studies' as appropriate when evaluating how STROBE is cited or applied in the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: assessing methodological quality
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE should not be used as a tool to assess the methodological quality of observational studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper identifies misuse particularly in systematic reviews and meta-analyses where STROBE is inappropriately applied as a study-quality assessment instrument (example: among 19 systematic reviews examined, 10 (53%) used STROBE inappropriately for quality assessment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: guideline for design and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE is not intended to be used as a guideline on how to design and conduct observational studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors list using STROBE to advise study design or conduct as an inappropriate application of the reporting guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of citation contexts for STROBE
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations of STROBE in the literature can be classified by article type/context (observational studies, systematic reviews including meta-analyses, comments/editorials/letters, methodological articles, recommendations and narrative reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the study's random sample of 100 articles citing STROBE: ~32% were observational studies, ~19% systematic reviews, 15% comments/editorials/letters, 8% methodological articles, and 26% recommendations/narrative reviews. This taxonomy can be used to interpret the meaning of STROBE citations and detect misuse.
